summary: Operation: Valhalla Journey (Low-Poly Edition) is an immersive, browser-based 3D space survival simulation built using HTML5, CSS3, vanilla JavaScript, and Three.js (r128). Players manage a high-stakes, 15-day solo mission aboard the VSS Astrid traveling to Kepler-186f, where they must assemble a scientific probe, execute landing sequences, collect planetary samples, and return safely to Earth.The project addresses space exploration challenges by transforming complex astrobiology and engineering concepts—grounded in NASA's Exoplanet Catalog and 3D Resources—into an interactive experience. Operating within strict three-minute daily cycles, players balance mandatory ship checks, waste control, emergency repairs, and finite resources (12 food and 12 water portions). Every skipped task directly impacts hull integrity and astronaut health. This simulation is important because it provides an accessible, zero-installation platform that educates students and space enthusiasts. By focusing on resource management rather than combat, it fosters a deeper appreciation for the real-world operational trade-offs and life-support logistics required in deep-space missions.
details: Operation: Valhalla Journey (Low-Poly Edition) is a single-player, browser-based 3D space survival simulation where players command a solo 15-day mission aboard the VSS Astrid to reach Kepler-186f, assemble and land a scientific probe, collect three mineral samples, and return safely to Earth. Working across real-time three-minute daily cycles, the game tasks players with balancing mandatory ship maintenance checks, waste disposal, emergency repairs, and finite rations (12 food and 12 water portions) where every skipped task or repair costs persistent health, hull integrity, or precious mission time. Built entirely with HTML5, CSS3, vanilla JavaScript, and Three.js (r128) alongside Web Audio synthesis—requiring zero backend servers, installations, or external asset packs—it evolves an original 2D retro prototype into an articulated, low-poly 3D environment complete with smooth wall-sliding physics, orbital gravity simulations, and interactive probe-landing cinematics. By shifting the focus of space games from combat to internal resource stewardship and life-support logistics, the project offers accessible, zero-barrier STEM education designed to help students and space enthusiasts intuitively grasp the real human and engineering trade-offs of deep-space exploration. Throughout development, our team prioritized offline-capable browser performance, cross-device responsiveness (supporting both desktop keyboard controls and mobile touch inputs), and clear visual/audio feedback loops so complex survival mechanics remain immediately readable under pressure.
